main_body: Sci-fi building: a pale blue-grey metal roof slab (rows 1-16) over a grey front wall (rows 18-43) with two cyan windows, two dark windows and a central door.
top_band: Roof slope in light blue-grey (L 148-178) at rows 1-16 with panel seams and vents. Its front edge is a pale line at rows 16-17 (L 178-201).
evidence: Column x=32 reads as an outline at row 0, then the roof at rows 1-16 (L 148-178, with seam rows at L 93). A pale front-edge line sits at row 17 (L 201), and a dark eave row at row 18 (L 67). An orange trim band at rows 19-23 follows, then the wall and door below. The roof is a large, clearly lighter top surface that steps abruptly to the vertical wall. The roof corners taper at the left and right, so the roof reads as a real top surface rather than a hat. The windows and door are framed with dark inner edges and sills, so they read as inset. No receding side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The roof has five lightness steps (178/148/118/93/70) with seam lines and vent details. The wall has panel seams, rivets, window glow gradients, sills and hazard stripes. Median colours per tile is 10, against 11 for the stone reference and 18 for the other. Flat-fill coverage is 4%, which is low. The 29 distinct colours is below both references (66 and 185), but the piece is small. The dark edge pixels are 76% neutral, which leans toward a black outline. The bluish dark tones on the wall and frames are tinted, so I call the outline mixed. Overall it is acceptable next to the references, though a little flatter and with less per-surface grain.
